before: Across the Wisconsin Breast Cancer and Pima Indians Diabetes datasets, federating a quantum model does not by itself distort its attributions under balanced client data: under independent and identically distributed partitions and under quantity skew, federated attributions stay in a low, tight band around their centralized references. Amplitude encoding gives the strongest two-dataset fidelity (Pima federated-versus-centralized Jensen-Shannon distance 0.201 against re-uploading's 0.335) and ties angle for the most stable round-to-round attribution ranking (Kendall's tau 0.94 at fifteen seeds), ahead of re-uploading (0.89) and IQP (0.86). Among functional runs on Wisconsin, moderate label skew is the most divergent regime for local-to-global explanation disagreement while quantity skew is indistinguishable from the balanced case. Releasing the explanation vectors is not free: direct membership-inference area under the curve reaches 0.53 to 0.67 across encodings, resolvably above chance for amplitude, IQP and re-uploading, and a four-budget calibrated Laplace-noise sweep shows that no single noise level brings all four encodings back to chance. The practical consequence is that explanation-release noise in a quantum federation must be calibrated per encoding rather than set once for the system.
after: Across the Wisconsin Breast Cancer and Pima Indians Diabetes datasets, federating a quantum model does not by itself distort its attributions under balanced client data: under independent and identically distributed partitions and under quantity skew, federated attributions stay in a low, tight band around their centralized references. Among functional runs on Wisconsin, moderate label skew is the most divergent regime for local-to-global explanation disagreement while quantity skew is indistinguishable from the balanced case. before: ESQFL is the closest prior work: a digital-twin-driven, explainable and secured quantum federated learning system for voltage stability assessment in smart grids, which uses Shapley values and differential privacy as components. The distinction from the present work lies in the question each asks of the Shapley analysis. ESQFL asks which client contributed, using Shapley values for participant valuation and reward allocation within the federation. This project asks whether a given explanation is trustworthy, decomposing that into whether the feature attribution is faithful to the federated model, stable across rounds, coherent between local and global models, and safe to release. ESQFL also applies differential privacy for system security; this work measures, per encoding, how much noise is actually required to suppress an explanation-based membership attack.

before: Each explained input carries a membership label - one if it is in the training set, zero if it is a held-out test point. A logistic attack classifier is fitted on the standardised per-sample attribution vectors of fifty members and fifty non-members, and leakage is measured by its five-fold stratified cross-validated area under the receiver operating characteristic curve:
AUCMIA = AUC( { ( gattack( φ̂(xj) ), ymem(j) ) }j=1..100 )	(3.13)
after: Each input has membership label one for a training record and zero for a test record. Fifty of each are explained against a common twenty-record training background disjoint from queried members. Standardization and logistic regression are fitted within each of five stratified outer training folds. The primary AUC is the arithmetic mean of held-out fold AUCs:
AUCMIA = (1/5) Σh=1..5 AUC(yIh, g-h(ΦIh))	(3.13)

before: 6.4 RQ4: MEMBERSHIP LEAKAGE THROUGH THE EXPLANATION VECTORS

At fifteen seeds under the balanced Wisconsin regime, the direct membership-inference area under the curve is 0.533 plus or minus 0.080 for angle, 0.620 plus or minus 0.112 for amplitude, 0.647 plus or minus 0.158 for IQP and 0.665 plus or minus 0.137 for re-uploading. Amplitude, IQP and re-uploading are each resolvably above angle, at 2.5, 2.5 and 3.2 standard errors respectively.

Measured against the chance level of one half, the mean is resolved beyond two standard errors for amplitude (4.2 standard errors), IQP (3.6) and re-uploading (4.7), but not for angle (1.6). Explanation-based membership leakage is therefore established for three of the four encodings and left at the boundary of chance for the fourth. The shadow-model variant of the attack fails for all four encodings, with means between 0.455 and 0.554: a shadow model trained without federation produces an explanation geometry that does not transfer to the federated target, so the direct attack is the appropriate instrument in this setting.

Two features of the direct attack qualify these values, and both are stated rather than buried. The attack classifier's feature standardisation is fitted on the pooled member and non-member set before cross-validation, so the absolute values are a mild over-estimate; this is uniform across encodings and seeds and does not affect the cross-encoding gaps or the angle-versus-chance test. And member explanations are computed against a training-set background while non-member explanations use a test-set background, so a portion of the measured separability could reflect train/test input distribution shift carried through the background rather than memorisation of members - although angle remaining at chance bounds that portion as small. The measured value is therefore best read as a test for the presence of a leakage signal rather than as an estimate of a realistic attacker's success rate.

Under non-balanced regimes on Wisconsin, three observations follow from Table 6.6. First, the five collapsed-run values all fall between 0.40 and 0.62, below the bulk of the functional values, consistent with - though at five samples not establishing - collapsed models leaking less. Second, quantity skew leaks somewhat more than severe label skew for amplitude and re-uploading but not for IQP, whose two settings are indistinguishable. Third, under quantity skew IQP and re-uploading are tied at 0.700, ahead of amplitude and angle; the single highest value in the whole non-balanced sweep is re-uploading at one seed under quantity skew, at 0.916, which is a seed-level observation rather than an encoding-level ranking.

6.5 RQ4: MITIGATION BY CALIBRATED RELEASE NOISE

The calibrated Laplace-noise sweep covers four encodings, four budgets and five seeds under the balanced Wisconsin regime. Noise is added to the attribution vectors after the fact, with the model held fixed across budgets for each encoding-seed pair, so the sweep traces the privacy-utility curve of explanation release rather than of a retrained private model.
Table 6.7  RQ4 direct attack area under the curve under calibrated Laplace noise across four budgets, balanced Wisconsin regime, five seeds per cell. A smaller budget means more noise.
after: Figure 6.3  Corrected direct-MIA AUC. Points and error bars show mean ± SD across fifteen IID targets; the dashed line is chance. No encoding has a resolved clean IID signal. This is an attack-specific signal probe, not a realistic attacker-success rate or a privacy guarantee.

Both member and non-member explanations now use the same twenty-record training-derived background, disjoint from the fifty queried members. Standardization and logistic regression are fitted only within training folds. The primary statistic is the mean of five held-out fold AUCs. Four inner training folds select score orientation and a TPR-minus-FPR threshold for a separate direction-aware evaluation. Scores, labels and fold assignments are retained. Historical shadow-model scores are not mixed with the corrected protocol.

Non-IID summaries retain Track-A targets only and require at least three. Angle under severe label skew is insufficient at one of five targets. The corrected results do not establish the previous quantity-skew leakage leadership or a stable encoding ranking. Pima non-IID attacks remain untested.
Table 6.6  Corrected Wisconsin non-IID direct-MIA AUC means. Parentheses give functional targets out of five; a dash denotes insufficient coverage, not zero.
6.5 RQ4: CALIBRATED RELEASE-NOISE EVALUATION

The corrected sweep evaluates four noise levels for each of five Wisconsin IID targets per encoding. Each full set of one hundred per-sample explanations receives an independently sampled noise matrix, without cross-group reuse. The target stays fixed across release settings. Utility is measured on the same clean/noisy records scored by the attack, rather than separately simulated averaged explanations.
Table 6.7  Corrected direct-MIA AUC under calibrated Laplace noise, mean ± SD across five Track-A targets per cell. Epsilon is a noise-level index, not a certified privacy budget.

before: Figure 6.4  RQ4 membership-inference signal under a calibrated Laplace-noise sweep, balanced Wisconsin regime, four encodings, five seeds per point. The attack area under the curve is recomputed after adding noise of the scale given by equation (3.14) per component; the four budgets are shown on a categorical axis, evenly spaced and not to scale, because only four values were tested. Lines are means and shaded bands are plus or minus one standard deviation. The dashed line is chance. The scale factor is an empirical attribution magnitude, not a certified sensitivity bound, and no formal privacy guarantee is claimed.

At the tightest budget all four encodings fall to between 0.311 and 0.331, uniformly near random. At a budget of one, angle falls to 0.415 while amplitude, re-uploading and IQP sit between 0.562 and 0.588. The attack strength rises monotonically with the budget for nineteen of twenty encoding-seed pairs; the single exception dips by 0.002 at the loosest budget, which is within permutation-sampling variance.

The deployment-relevant consequence is stated plainly: no single budget brings all encodings equally close to chance. Bringing all four to near-chance requires the tightest budget tested, which also destroys most of the utility of the explanation. A deployment that set its budget to one on the strength of angle's response alone would leave the other three encodings roughly fifteen points higher than it believed.

Answer to RQ4. The released explanation vectors do carry training-set membership information: leakage is resolved above chance for amplitude, IQP and re-uploading, and sits at the boundary of chance for angle. Calibrated release noise suppresses that leakage unevenly across encodings, and no single budget is simultaneously adequate for all four. Noise calibration for explanation release must therefore be per-encoding.
after: Figure 6.4  Corrected calibrated Laplace-noise response. Points and error bars give raw direct-MIA AUC mean ± SD across five targets, with categorical tested indices and a chance line at 0.5. No monotonic mitigation is established. The empirical scale is not a certified sensitivity bound; no formal privacy guarantee is claimed.

The sweep does not reproduce the earlier monotonic suppression claim. The isolated IQP cell at epsilon = 1 has AUC 0.561 ± 0.051, approximately 2.65 standard errors above chance in an unadjusted comparison; it is exploratory, not a stable ranking. Matched cosine utility spans 0.013–0.063 at epsilon = 0.1 and 0.701–0.829 at epsilon = 5. Stronger noise degrades the explanation, but clean baselines already lack a resolved signal, so successful mitigation is not established.

Post-hoc max(AUC, 1-AUC) is an orientation diagnostic, not a validated attack score. Attack advantage is held-out TPR minus FPR at a training-selected threshold; negative estimates are retained. With fifty non-members, pooled empirical FPR resolution is 0.02. Low-FPR ROC values are descriptive and do not validate one-percent-FPR guarantees.

Answer to RQ4: the evaluated attack does not establish clean IID membership discrimination or an encoding-dependent leakage ranking. The matched release experiment measures utility degradation but establishes neither effective privacy mitigation nor formal differential privacy.

before: Noise calibration must be per encoding. The budget that brings angle to near-chance leaves the other three encodings' leakage largely intact, and bringing all four to near-chance requires a much tighter budget that also degrades the explanation's usefulness. A noise level tuned on one encoding does not transfer to another.

Explanation release carries a measurable privacy cost. That cost is present across all encodings and under both balanced and skewed data, even when the model itself is considered safe to deploy. The explanation is a second release channel and has to be governed as one.
after: No effective privacy budget is established. The corrected attack has no resolved clean IID signal. Noise decreases attribution utility, but the evaluation does not justify a deployment protection rule.
A null attack is not a privacy certificate. Stronger attacks, independent reference data and larger evaluation samples may detect risks not resolved by this logistic-regression probe.

before: Two of these deserve emphasis because they are the ones a deployment would act on. The first is that explanation release is a distinct privacy channel with a distinct, measurable cost, and that the noise required to close it differs by encoding - so a budget tuned once for a system is the wrong design. The second is that a collapsed model still returns a confident-looking explanation, and that a production release path needs a functional-model gate or it will present degeneracy as insight.
after: Two limitations matter for deployment: a null result from one attack family is not a privacy guarantee, and collapsed models require a functional-model gate before standard attribution comparisons.

before: The membership attack is a signal-presence proxy. It is trained and cross-validated on the same target model's labelled explanations, its standardisation is fitted on the pooled set, and member and non-member explanations use different backgrounds. Absolute values are therefore a mild over-estimate; the cross-encoding ranking and angle's position at chance are robust to both effects.
after: The membership attack is a signal-presence proxy. The corrected pipeline fits standardization within training folds and uses one common training-derived background. The attack still uses labelled explanations from the same target, and only one attack family with one hundred queried records is evaluated. A null result does not establish privacy.
